exposure: Indication for operative delivery (dystocia vs. fetal distress)
Midcavity operative vaginal delivery (forceps, vacuum, sequential)
Type of operative vaginal delivery (forceps, vacuum, sequential)
outcome: Severe perinatal morbidity/mortality (e.g., convulsions, severe birth trauma, perinatal death)
Severe maternal morbidity (e.g., severe postpartum hemorrhage, shock, sepsis, cardiac complications)
cohort: Women with term, singleton deliveries in British Columbia, Canada, from 2004 to 2014, who underwent attempted midcavity operative vaginal delivery or cesarean delivery in the second stage of labor
finding: Attempted midcavity operative vaginal delivery is associated with higher rates of severe perinatal morbidity/mortality and severe maternal morbidity compared to cesarean delivery, with varying effects depending on the indication for delivery and the instrument used.
mod_finding: The study found increased risks of severe outcomes associated with different modes of midcavity operative vaginal delivery depending on the indication. For dystocia, all types of midcavity operative vaginal delivery (forceps, vacuum, sequential) were associated with higher risks of both perinatal and maternal complications compared to cesarean delivery. For fetal distress, attempted midcavity vacuum was associated with increased perinatal morbidity/mortality, while attempted midcavity forceps delivery was linked to increased maternal morbidity.
